rationale.conceptual: The method applies established topological defect concepts from liquid crystals and Eshelby inclusion fitting to amorphous solids; it involves several interacting components (MD, coarse-graining, winding number calculation, phase-shift analysis, non-linear fitting) and non-trivial equations, requiring careful implementation but not a brand-new algorithm.
rationale.execution: The pipeline spans glass generation, long AQS MD runs (50000 strain steps per sample), multiple post-processing stages (displacement calculation, defect detection, fitting), and metric computation; while the reference solve script condenses into a single Python script, orchestrating the MD simulations and analysis correctly is a multi-stage effort with dependencies on external tool (LAMMPS).

difficulty.reasoning: The task reproduces a topological defect analysis pipeline combining MD simulations, coarse-graining, defect detection, and Eshelby inclusion fitting; while the individual concepts are published methods, their integration requires careful implementation of non-trivial equations and multi-step numerical analysis.

compute_estimate.reasoning: MD simulations of 10,000-atom 2D glasses under AQS shear up to 0.5 strain run on CPU; memory and data volumes are modest (a few GB).
